examples.ko: 칡으로 만든 차를 마셔 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever tried tea made from kudzu?
We dug up kudzu in the mountains and made juice.
Grandfather is resting while chewing on kudzu root.

examples.ko: 칡은 쓴맛이 강하지만 몸에 좋다고 해요.
examples.en: Kudzu tastes quite bitter, but they say it is good for you.

examples.ko: 시골 마당에 칡이 길게 뻗어 있어요.
examples.en: Kudzu is stretching out long across the yard in the countryside.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 칡 줄기로 줄넘기를 했어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I jumped rope with kudzu stems.

explain: 칡은 뿌리로 즙, 차, 냉면 같은 음식을 만들어서 먹거리 이야기에 자주 나와요. 한의학에서는 칡뿌리를 '갈근'이라고도 해요. 줄기는 '칡덩굴'이라고 따로 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: Kudzu roots are used for juice, tea and even cold noodles, so the word often comes up when talking about food. In traditional Korean medicine the root is also called '갈근'. The vines are sometimes called '칡덩굴' separately.

examples.en: My salivary gland was swollen, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 레몬 사진만 봐도 침샘이 자극되는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I feel like my salivary glands get stimulated just by looking at a picture of a lemon.

examples.ko: 침샘은 입 안에 침을 만들어 줘요.
examples.en: The salivary glands produce saliva in your mouth.
As you get older, salivary gland function gets weaker.
I got an infection in my salivary gland, so I took antibiotics.

examples.ko: 입이 마르는 건 침샘 때문일 수도 있대요.
examples.en: They say a dry mouth can be caused by the salivary glands.

explain: '침샘이 자극되다'는 맛있는 음식이나 신 음식을 보고 입에 침이 고일 때 써요. 일상에서는 '침이 고이다'라고 더 많이 말하고, '침샘'은 건강이나 몸 이야기에서 나와요.
explain_en: '침샘이 자극되다' is used when delicious or sour food makes your mouth water. In daily talk people more often say '침이 고이다', while '침샘' appears in health and body topics.

examples.ko: 그 기사는 작은 일을 침소봉대한 거예요.
examples.en: That article blew a small matter way out of proportion.
Please don't blow a small mistake out of proportion.
There is criticism that the media exaggerates the incident.
That's just exaggeration. It's nothing serious.
Rumors are easily blown out of proportion.
My friend passed on what I said after blowing it out of proportion.

explain: '과장하다'보다 딱딱해서 뉴스나 토론에서 남의 말이나 보도를 비판할 때 많이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '부풀리다'나 '뻥튀기하다'처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than '과장하다' (to exaggerate) and is often used in news or debates when criticizing someone's words or reporting. In daily conversation people also say '부풀리다' or '뻥튀기하다'.

examples.en: I received acupuncture treatment at a Korean medicine clinic.

examples.ko: 할머니는 어깨가 아파서 침술 치료를 받으셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother's shoulder hurt, so she received acupuncture treatment.

examples.ko: 침술은 동양 의학에서 오래 쓰인 방법이에요.
examples.en: Acupuncture is a method used for a long time in Eastern medicine.

examples.ko: 한의과 대학에서 침술을 배우는 학생이 많아요.
examples.en: Many students at colleges of Korean medicine learn acupuncture.
That person is famous for being excellent at acupuncture.

examples.ko: 외국에서도 침술에 관심을 갖는 사람이 늘었어요.
examples.en: Even abroad, more people are interested in acupuncture.

explain: '침술'은 침을 놓는 기술이나 치료법을 말할 때 써요. 병원에 가는 일상 대화에서는 '침 맞으러 가다', '침을 놓다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: '침술' is used when talking about the skill or method of treatment with needles. In everyday talk about going to a clinic, people say '침 맞으러 가다' (to go get acupuncture) or '침을 놓다' (to give acupuncture).

examples.ko: 산 위쪽에는 침엽수림이 넓게 펼쳐져 있어요.
examples.en: A coniferous forest spreads widely on the upper part of the mountain.

examples.ko: 침엽수림은 겨울에도 푸른 잎이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Coniferous forests keep their green needles even in winter.
We walked along a path through the coniferous forest.
We picked up pine cones in the coniferous forest.
During my trip to Northern Europe, I passed through a coniferous forest.
There are many pine and fir trees in a coniferous forest.

explain: 반대말은 '활엽수림'이고, 줄여서 '침엽수'라고도 해요. 지리나 과학 수업, 여행 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: The opposite is '활엽수림' (broadleaf forest), and the shorter form '침엽수' (conifer) is also used. It often comes up in geography and science classes and in travel talk.

examples.ko: 그는 슬픔 속에 깊이 침잠해 있어요.
examples.en: He is sunk deep in sadness.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나고 한동안 책 읽기에 침잠했어요.
examples.en: After the exam ended, I immersed myself in reading for a while.
When you sink into your thoughts, time goes by fast.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 조용한 음악 속에 침잠하고 싶대요.
examples.en: They say that singer wants to immerse himself in quiet music.

examples.ko: 분위기가 무겁게 침잠해서 아무도 말하지 않았어요.
examples.en: The mood sank heavily, so nobody spoke.

examples.ko: 마음이 침잠할 때는 산책이 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: When your mind sinks low, a walk helps.

explain: '슬픔에 침잠하다', '독서에 침잠하다'처럼 '~에' 뒤에 써요. 글에서 많이 쓰는 말이라서 말할 때는 '가라앉다', '푹 빠지다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is used after '~에', as in '슬픔에 침잠하다' (sink into sorrow) or '독서에 침잠하다' (immerse oneself in reading). It is mostly a written word, so in speech '가라앉다' or '푹 빠지다' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 물에 소금을 너무 많이 넣으면 침전이 생겨요.
examples.en: If you put too much salt in water, sediment forms.
To prevent settling, keep stirring it.
Water purification goes through settling and filtering.

examples.ko: 침전 후에 맑은 윗물만 따라 내세요.
examples.en: After it settles, pour off only the clear water on top.

examples.ko: 이 물질은 침전에 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: This substance takes a long time to settle.
I strained out the residue formed by settling.

explain: 과학 수업이나 물을 깨끗하게 하는 과정을 설명할 때 많이 써요. 일상에서는 '가라앉다'라고 말하고, 가라앉은 것은 '앙금'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is common in science classes and when explaining how water is purified. In daily talk people say '가라앉다' (to sink or settle), and what settles at the bottom can also be called '앙금'.

examples.en: Sediment has built up at the bottom of the cup.
If you leave it alone, the sediment settles at the bottom.

examples.ko: 병 속 침전물을 조심해서 따라 내세요.
examples.en: Carefully pour out the sediment in the bottle.

examples.ko: 강바닥 침전물로 옛 환경을 알 수 있대요.
examples.en: They say you can learn about the past environment from riverbed sediment.
The water looks cloudy because of the sediment.
This filter easily gets clogged by sediment.

explain: 가라앉은 찌꺼기를 일상에서는 '앙금'이나 '찌꺼기'라고 말하기도 해요. '침전물'은 실험이나 물, 약품 이야기처럼 조금 설명하는 말투에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: In daily life people may also call settled leftovers '앙금' or '찌꺼기'. '침전물' appears more in explanatory contexts such as experiments, water and chemicals.

examples.ko: 눈이 침침해서 작은 글씨가 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: My eyes are blurry, so I can't see small print well.
The room is dim, so I'll turn on the light.
Lately my eyes keep getting blurry.
A dim alley is scary to walk through at night.

examples.ko: 나이가 들어서 눈이 침침하다고 할머니가 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother said her eyes have gotten blurry with age.

examples.ko: 침침할 때는 눈을 잠깐 쉬게 해 주세요.
examples.en: When your eyes feel blurry, let them rest for a moment.

explain: '눈이 침침하다'는 시력이 흐릿하고 답답할 때 자주 쓰고, 어두침침한 장소에도 써요. 그냥 '어둡다'보다 흐릿하고 답답한 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: '눈이 침침하다' is often used when your eyesight feels hazy and heavy, and it can also describe a gloomy place. It has a hazier, stuffier feel than simply '어둡다' (dark).

en: invade and plunder; encroach upon by force

examples.ko: 열강은 힘으로 약한 나라의 자원을 침탈했어요.
examples.en: The great powers plundered the resources of weaker countries by force.

examples.ko: 강대국이 약한 나라의 주권을 침탈하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Powerful countries must not seize the sovereignty of weak countries.

examples.ko: 역사 수업에서 열강이 어떻게 침탈했는지 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class we learned how the great powers plundered other countries.

examples.ko: 농민의 땅을 침탈한 관리가 벌을 받았어요.
examples.en: The official who seized the farmers' land was punished.

examples.ko: 다른 나라의 영토를 침탈하려는 시도는 비판받아요.
examples.en: Attempts to seize another country's territory are criticized.
They even took over the culture, so the backlash was big.

explain: '침략하다'는 군대로 쳐들어가는 데 초점이 있고, '침탈하다'는 힘으로 빼앗는 데 초점이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고 역사 수업이나 뉴스 같은 글에서 나와요.
explain_en: '침략하다' focuses on invading with an army, while '침탈하다' focuses on taking things away by force. It is rarely used in everyday talk and appears in history classes and news-style writing.

examples.en: The faces of the family were all grief-stricken.
The meeting began in a somber atmosphere.
He bowed his head in deep grief.
The players looked devastated at the news of the defeat.
The mood was one that the word 'mournful' fits exactly.

examples.ko: 침통할 때는 위로의 말도 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: When someone is grieving, you have to be careful even with words of comfort.

explain: '슬프다'보다 무겁고 조용한 슬픔을 말하고, 표정이나 분위기를 설명할 때 많이 써요. 뉴스에서 '침통한 표정'이라는 말이 자주 나와요. 자기 기분을 말할 때는 '슬퍼요'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It describes a heavier, quieter sadness than '슬프다' and is often used for facial expressions or atmosphere. The phrase '침통한 표정' (grief-stricken face) often appears in the news. When talking about your own feelings, '슬퍼요' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 그는 오랜 칩거 끝에 다시 모습을 보였어요.
examples.en: He appeared again after a long period of seclusion.
If the seclusion goes on long, your mind gets worn out too.

examples.ko: 작가는 칩거에 들어간 뒤 소설을 썼어요.
examples.en: The writer wrote a novel after going into seclusion.
I ended my time shut in and met a friend after a long while.

examples.ko: 한 달간의 칩거로 살이 많이 쪘어요.
examples.en: I gained a lot of weight from a month of staying shut in.
I'm worried about my neighbor who is shut away at home.

explain: 뉴스에서 정치인이나 작가, 연예인이 '칩거에 들어가다'라고 많이 써요. 일상에서는 '집에만 있다', '집에 틀어박히다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: In the news it is often used as '칩거에 들어가다' (to go into seclusion) for politicians, writers or celebrities. In daily talk people say '집에만 있다' or '집에 틀어박히다'.

en: live a secluded life; stick to home

examples.en: During exam period I shut myself in at home and studied.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 몇 달째 칩거하고 있어요.
examples.en: That actor has been living in seclusion for several months.
It was cold, so I stayed shut in at home all weekend.
If you shut yourself away, meeting people gets even harder.
I went into the mountains looking for a place to live in seclusion.

examples.ko: 작가가 칩거하는 동안 새 책이 나왔어요.
examples.en: A new book came out while the writer was living in seclusion.

explain: 일상에서는 '집에 틀어박히다', '집에만 있다'가 더 자연스럽고, '칩거하다'는 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 써요. 가볍게 주말에 집에 있었던 일에 쓰면 조금 과장된 느낌이에요.
explain_en: In daily talk '집에 틀어박히다' or '집에만 있다' sounds more natural, while '칩거하다' is common in writing and the news. Using it for simply staying home on a weekend sounds a bit exaggerated.

en: fussing; whining (of a baby or small child)

examples.en: The baby is fussing, probably because it's sleepy.
My little brother has been whining and pestering since morning.
The child is fretting and throwing a tantrum.

examples.ko: 아기가 밤새 칭얼칭얼 울어서 한숨도 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The baby fussed and cried all night, so I didn't sleep a wink.

examples.ko: 열이 나는지 아이가 칭얼칭얼 보채서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: The child is fretful, maybe from a fever, and I'm worried.
I can hear fussy crying from the next room.

explain: 아기나 어린아이가 졸리거나 아파서 낮은 소리로 계속 보챌 때 써요. '엉엉'은 크게 우는 소리고, '칭얼칭얼'은 짜증 섞인 소리가 이어지는 느낌이에요. 어른에게 쓰면 어린아이 같다고 놀리는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when a baby or small child keeps fussing in a low voice because of sleepiness or discomfort. '엉엉' is loud crying, while '칭얼칭얼' feels like a continuous, cranky whimper. Using it for adults sounds like teasing them for being childish.

en: round and round; wrapped tightly in many layers

examples.en: I wrapped a scarf around my neck many times.
I wound a bandage tightly around his arm.
I tied the rope around the post in many loops.
The yarn got tangled around the chair leg in coils.
It was cold, so I wrapped a blanket around myself layer after layer.
Try to untangle the wire that is coiled round and round.

explain: 줄, 끈, 붕대, 목도리처럼 길고 가는 것을 여러 겹 둘러 감는 모습에 써요. 보통 '감다', '두르다', '묶다'와 함께 나와요. '친친'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: It describes wrapping something long and thin, like rope, string, a bandage or a scarf, around something in many layers. It usually appears with '감다', '두르다' or '묶다'. '친친' is used with the same meaning.

examples.en: Grandmother's voice is still clear and sharp.
The teacher called attendance in a high, ringing voice.
His voice was so high and clear that I could hear it from far away.
That announcer speaks in a high, clear voice.
The ringing voice suddenly became quiet.

examples.ko: 카랑카랑할 만큼 높은 목소리라 귀가 아파요.
examples.en: The voice is so high and sharp that my ears hurt.

explain: 주로 목소리가 높고 맑으면서 힘 있게 울릴 때 써요. '낭랑하다'가 부드럽고 듣기 좋은 느낌이라면, '카랑카랑하다'는 조금 날카롭게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is mainly used when a voice is high, clear and rings out with strength. While '낭랑하다' feels soft and pleasant to hear, '카랑카랑하다' can sound a little sharp.

examples.ko: 슬픈 영화를 보고 울고 나니 카타르시스를 느꼈어요.
examples.en: After watching a sad movie and crying, I felt a catharsis.
I go to karaoke to feel a release of emotions.
The ending of this drama was hugely cathartic.

examples.ko: 카타르시스는 비극을 볼 때 생긴다고 해요.
examples.en: They say catharsis arises when you watch a tragedy.
The audience got a sense of catharsis from the final twist.

examples.ko: 카타르시스 효과가 있는 글쓰기를 해 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried a kind of writing that has a cathartic effect.

explain: 영화, 드라마, 노래 같은 것을 보거나 하면서 쌓인 감정이 시원하게 풀릴 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '속이 후련하다', '시원하다'라고 하고, 드라마에서 속이 시원해지는 전개는 '사이다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when watching films, dramas or listening to songs lets built-up emotions come out and leaves you relieved. In daily talk people say '속이 후련하다' or '시원하다', and a satisfying plot turn in a drama is also called '사이다'.

en: choke; gasp; make a choking sound

examples.en: Food got stuck in my throat and I choked and coughed.
There is a lot of dust, so the kids are coughing and choking.
Even while choking and coughing, I kept drinking water.

examples.ko: 급하게 먹다가 캑캑거리지 않게 천천히 드세요.
examples.en: Eat slowly so that you don't choke from eating in a hurry.
The cat hacked and then spat out a hairball.
I helped a person who was coughing and choking from breathing in smoke.

explain: 목이 막히거나 먼지, 연기 때문에 숨이 막혀 '캑캑' 소리를 낼 때 써요. 음식이 잘못 넘어가서 기침이 나올 때는 '사레들리다'라고도 해요. 감기 기침은 '콜록콜록'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when you make a 'kaek-kaek' sound because something blocks your throat, or dust or smoke makes it hard to breathe. When food goes down the wrong way and makes you cough, people also say '사레들리다'. A cold cough is '콜록콜록'.

examples.en: The neighbor's dog is barking loudly.

examples.ko: 밤새 컹컹 소리가 들려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep because I heard barking all night.

examples.ko: 낯선 사람이 오자 개가 컹컹 짖기 시작했어요.
examples.en: When a stranger came, the dog started barking.
I woke up startled by the sound of barking.

examples.ko: 멀리서 컹컹 울리는 개 소리가 들렸어요.
examples.en: I heard a dog's deep bark echoing from far away.

examples.ko: 우리 집 개는 택배 아저씨만 보면 컹컹 짖어요.
examples.en: Our dog barks whenever it sees the delivery man.

explain: 주로 덩치가 큰 개가 낮고 울리는 소리로 짖는 소리예요. 가장 일반적인 개 소리는 '멍멍'이고, 강아지가 놀라거나 아파서 내는 소리는 '캥캥'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It imitates the low, resonant bark of a mainly large dog. The most general dog sound is '멍멍', and the yelp a puppy makes when startled or hurt is '캥캥'.
